PullRequest.Title: mcp: add chat.mcp.workspaceServersEnabled to gate repository-defined MCP servers
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #338958

## Why

A repository can ship MCP server configuration (`.vscode/mcp.json`, a root `.mcp.json`, the `mcp` section of a `.code-workspace`), and those servers run their `command` as soon as the folder is opened or an agent session starts in it. Workspace Trust is the only control today, and it is all-or-nothing: people grant it to get tasks, debugging and extensions working. `chat.mcp.access` can turn MCP off entirely but does not distinguish who configured a server. #338958 asks to disable workspace servers while keeping user servers; the same request is open against the CLI (github/copilot-cli#3380, github/copilot-cli#3419).

## What

- New setting `chat.mcp.workspaceServersEnabled` (boolean, default `true`, `APPLICATION` scope). When `false`, workspace-configured servers stay listed but do not start, do not autostart, and provide no tools. User, extension, plugin and built-in servers are unaffected. Applies to the local harness and to Copilot, Claude and Codex sessions in the Agent Host.
- Per-workspace override: the setting is the class decision. The Workspace group header in the MCP servers list of the Customizations editor gets a toggle that enables or disables the class for this workspace. Overrides live in editor-owned storage (workspace storage locally, Agent Host storage for sessions), never in the repository. Per-server Workspace and Session decisions still work on top.
- Per-server Global ("Enable" for the profile) is not offered for a gated workspace server: that decision is keyed by server name and would leak across repositories. The row switch of a gated server moves its Workspace or Session override instead.
- Reading or watching an `mcp-resource:` URI (for example an image in a Markdown preview) no longer starts a disabled server; this applies to every disabled server, not only gated ones.

Why a repository cannot reopen the gate:

- `APPLICATION` scope: only local user settings can set the key. Workspace, folder and `.code-workspace` settings are dropped, and so are the remote user settings a dev container ships.
- Overrides are written only through the UI: the local model directly, and the host through the `vscode/setWorkspaceMcpServersEnablement` extension method on a direct, non-relay connection. No command is registered, and the host checks that a Workspace decision names the session's own working directory.
- A server's origin is decided by whoever read its configuration (VS Code for `.vscode/mcp.json`, the host's own scan for `.mcp.json`, the Copilot runtime's self-reported source) and travels as `source: 'workspace'` metadata. When VS Code forwards `.vscode/mcp.json` servers to the host in its client bundle, the source goes with them (`vscode.mcpServerSources`), so they are gated on the host like host-discovered servers.

Per harness:

- Local: `WorkspaceMcpServersEnablementModel` sits below the collision model, so a gated workspace server never counts as an enabled collision partner. Dev-mode autostart and the MCP gateway (`vscode.lm.startMcpGateway`) no longer start disabled servers.
- Agent Host: `AgentHostCustomizationEnablementService` resolves workspace-configured targets as `session > workspace > setting`. `WorkspaceMcpServersContribution` publishes the class decision in the session `_meta` (`vscode.workspaceMcpServers`) for sessions that have workspace-sourced servers.
- Copilot: host-discovered `.mcp.json` servers and forwarded `.vscode/mcp.json` servers go out as `disabledMcpServers` at launch, so the runtime never starts them.
- Claude: project `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.mcp.json` servers are stamped `workspace`, `~/.claude/settings.json` servers `user`; gated servers are passed as `deniedMcpServers` at launch and stay listed (stopped) after the session starts. Only the primary working directory is scanned.
- Codex: `.mcp.json` declarations are listed before Codex starts them, withheld ones as stopped. Closing the gate marks an established thread for reload rather than stopping its servers: a server still running keeps its workspace origin and is published disabled until the thread reloads. A client plugin that declares a server name owns it whether or not the plugin is enabled, as in the Copilot harness.

## How to test

1. Settings: uncheck `Chat > MCP: Workspace Servers Enabled`.
2. Open a folder with a `.vscode/mcp.json` or `.mcp.json`. Chat > Customizations > MCP Servers: the Workspace group lists its servers disabled ("disabled by the setting"); they do not start and offer no tools.
3. Click the toggle on the Workspace group header: the servers of this workspace become enabled, persisted for this workspace only. Click again to disable.
4. Agents window: create a Copilot session in the same folder. Same list and toggle; per-server `Enable (Session)` remains available.
5. Re-check the setting: previous behavior is restored.

Captioned recordings of the Copilot-harness flows (VS Code window, Agents window, local harness) exist and can be attached on request.

## Validation

```
pnpm run typecheck-client                                   # clean
node build/eslint.ts <changed files>                        # clean
pnpm run valid-layers-check                                 # clean
./scripts/test.bat --glob "**/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js"
./scripts/test.bat --glob "**/contrib/mcp/test/**/*.test.js"
./scripts/test.bat --glob "**/aiCustomization/**/*.test.js"
./scripts/test.bat --glob "**/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/**/*.test.js"
./scripts/test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness.test.ts
```

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| agentHost | 18,878 passing, 101 pending, 19 failing: the `SessionPermissionManager` cases fail identically on clean `origin/main` in this environment |
| contrib/mcp | 510 passing, 15 pending |
| aiCustomization | 1,022 passing |
| chat agentSessions | 3,460 passing, 2 pending |
| remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness | 18 passing |

Not exercised: live Claude/Codex SDK flows, remote (tunnel/SSH) agent hosts, Settings Sync of the `APPLICATION`-scoped key. Whether the Claude runtime loads `mcpServers` from project settings files is taken from the existing scanner, not verified against the SDK.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Plugin-bundled servers of repository-enabled plugins (Claude `@skills-dir` plugins enabled from `.claude/settings.json`; Codex's trusted-project `.codex/config.toml`) are governed by the plugin or by Codex, not by this gate.
- Repository-defined hooks are the same risk class; the Copilot SDK already has `enableFileHooks`.
- The class is decided for the session's primary folder but applies to servers from every anchored root; worktree sessions do not inherit the repository's Workspace decision.
- A host that has not received the mirrored setting treats the class as enabled; on a shared remote host the last connected client's value wins.
- Claude still loads MCP servers declared in on-disk agent frontmatter, which the host does not scan.
- Policy exposure of the setting.
- Withholding is by server name. A repository server named like a user or built-in server (Claude `deniedMcpServers`, Copilot `disabledMcpServers`) withholds that server too; same-named servers already merge by name in those runtimes.
- Opting a workspace in trusts the workspace, not a configuration: later edits to its MCP files take effect on the next start without a prompt, as they do today.
- Servers a dev container provisions through `customizations.vscode.mcp` land in the remote user `mcp.json` and count as user servers, as do `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and Codex `config.toml` servers.
- A host without the `vscode.workspaceMcpServers` capability (an older remote host) keeps workspace servers enabled; the toggle is hidden there.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The duplicate call path, exact four-file serial loop, and placement before sdkService.startup are directly established in repository code. Only the absolute latency varies by filesystem.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem read operations and JSON parsing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is four serial read attempts per materialization/rematerialization and grows with filesystem latency and the number of SDK restarts; three of those reads are discarded by the subsequent workspace/non-.mcp.json filter.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased first-response and rematerialization latency from repeated blocking filesystem I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, session creation scanned Claude MCP declarations for the customization snapshot, while _buildExternalMcpServers proceeded from the cached SessionMcpDiscovery/client-plugin inputs without rescanning Claude settings files.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Claude startup now calls scanClaudeMcpServers inside _buildExternalMcpServers before SDK startup, even though AgentService session creation has already requested getSessionCustomizations, which runs the same scan.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added await at line 927 introduces a second scan in _buildExternalMcpServers; no equivalent filesystem scan existed on this startup path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Reuse the MCP scan before starting Claude
Findings.Impact: On the first Claude message, and again on every SDK rematerialization, four serial file reads now block SDK startup and therefore delay the first response. The delay is especially visible when the workspace or home directory is on a remote or high-latency filesystem.
Findings.Evidence: AgentService.createSession awaits provider.getChatCustomizations before publishing the session; ClaudeAgentSession.getSessionCustomizations calls scanClaudeMcpServers. The added line calls it again from _buildStartupToolWiring's critical path. scanClaudeMcpServers loops serially over workspace .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .mcp.json, and user ~/.claude/settings.json, and readJsonFile performs fileService.readFile even for missing files. _buildStartupToolWiring is used for both initial materialization and rematerialization.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache/coalesce the session's Claude MCP scan and reuse the snapshot produced for initial customizations, invalidating it from the existing customization watchers; at minimum, avoid rescanning the discarded .mcp.json and user settings files and read only the two project settings files together.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create an Agent Host session and publish its initial customization inventory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentService.createSession waits for provider.getChatCustomizations before publishing the initial session state, so provider discovery is on session-creation latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Claude workspace/user MCP configuration files and parse JSONC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four serial read attempts for a session with a working directory, including missing files
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initial Claude customization snapshot already performed this scan; the PR adds settings.local.json to the existing candidate list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the initial customization snapshot and therefore session publication

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold read per distinct root, parallel across roots; warm calls use shared cached snapshots
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The customization-read path did not force MCP discovery; later launch/send paths already refreshed the same shared discovery, so this generally moves the single cold read earlier rather than adding another read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now blocks initial Codex customization publication so declarations can be listed before Codex starts

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workspace roots, customization files, plugins, and MCP declarations; effective MCP file cardinality is one declaration file per Codex root and four Claude MCP candidate files for the primary root/home.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentService runs customization discovery and folder-picker computation in parallel. Claude runs its different customization scanners in parallel, but scanClaudeMcpServers reads its four candidate files serially. Codex SessionMcpDiscovery reads roots in parallel and coalesces/caches each root through a shared sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Codex root discovery is shared by file-service/root and warm refreshes return cached definitions until watcher invalidation. Claude's MCP scan has no cache and reads every candidate on each invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call paths, serial/parallel behavior, and cache ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote filesystem latency and the number of roots vary, but Codex coalescing prevents repeated cold reads and Claude's initial scan was already required.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for initial publication: the new Codex read is cached, bounded by roots, and intentionally moves required discovery before publication.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first Claude message or rematerialize its SDK pipeline
Scenarios.CriticalPath: _buildStartupToolWiring awaits _buildExternalMcpServers, including the added MCP scan, before buildOptions and sdkService.startup; all added reads directly block first-response progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four serial read attempts per initial SDK materialization and per rematerialization; three results are discarded by the subsequent filter
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Startup used SessionMcpDiscovery and client-plugin data without rescanning these four Claude settings files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays sdkService.startup and thus the first response/recovery

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the GitHub MCP endpoint when configured
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per startup wiring build
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already preceded external-server construction and remains on the same startup path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or rebuild the Claude SDK query process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup per materialization or recovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The subprocess startup existed but was not preceded by the duplicate Claude MCP scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cannot begin until the newly added serial scan completes

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Materialization/rematerialization count and filesystem latency; four candidate files per invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four reads inside scanClaudeMcpServers are serialized by a for/await loop. The scan is not coalesced with the scan already completed during session creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No positive, negative, or in-flight cache exists for scanClaudeMcpServers; missing files are retried and an identical scan occurs on every rematerialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: duplicate scans and their placement before SDK startup are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Absolute delay depends on local versus remote/home filesystem latency and restart frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated filesystem work on a response-critical path; submitted one medium-severity finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or resume a Codex session with workspace MCP declarations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MCP discovery must complete before thread configuration is built; on first customization publication the PR can perform the cold read earlier, while materialize/send then observe the cached snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read .mcp.json for each effective workspace root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold read per root, parallel across roots; watcher-triggered rereads only after changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery already ran from materialize/send; the diff adds an earlier caller but reuses the same cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before thread/start configuration; the diff's customization call usually warms the same cache used later

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start/resume Codex thread with filtered mcp_servers configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Thread startup existed; the PR changes filtering/provenance and withholds gated workspace servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Consumes cached discovery and starts only enabled workspace servers

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct workspace roots and MCP declaration count after name deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Roots refresh concurrently; each root has a shared sequencer, and session merges are sequenced. Codex process RPC remains serialized through the app-server client.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold read once per root, warm refresh uses _initialized snapshots, file watchers force rescans, and discoveries are shared while referenced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: cache, watcher, and launch paths are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repositories with many roots are less common, but reads are parallel and shared.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new early refresh does not multiply cold filesystem calls because root discovery is shared and cached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle workspace-server enablement from the Customizations editor or Agent Host UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click sends one enablement update; the host persists the workspace/session decision and republishes session metadata before the UI reflects it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode/setWorkspaceMcpServersEnablement from renderer to Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The click awaits the host update

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the resolved class decision in session _meta and synchronize state to clients
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one changed metadata publication per affected session; equals suppresses duplicates
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No workspace-MCP class metadata was published.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for UI consistency after the decision changes

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded storage update per durable workspace override
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of applying the toggle, with no collection fan-out

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user action and one target session; setting-level changes notify all initialized sessions, while per-workspace/session overrides affect one session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited extension request per click. Host persistence and metadata publication are synchronous/sequenced through existing state services; equality guards suppress unchanged metadata writes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace decisions persist in workspace/host storage; session decisions live in session state. Resolved metadata is cached in session state and compared before publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request cardinality and equality guards are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session counts affect setting-flip notification fan-out, but user-triggered flips are rare and unchanged decisions are suppressed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new boundaries are one-per-action, bounded, and necessary to persist and publish the decision.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use local MCP autostart, dev mode, gateway tools, or mcp-resource URIs while a server is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enablement is checked before starting or calling a server. Disabled-server paths terminate before subprocess, IPC, or resource reads; enabled-server paths retain existing behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for disabled servers; existing per-server starts for enabled servers
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dev mode could start/restart a disabled server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes disabled-server subprocess work

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List/call tools through the MCP gateway
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing request per gateway operation; disabled servers are filtered before lookup/start
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Gateway operations could reach disabled servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds only an in-memory enablement check and avoids disabled-server starts

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/watch an mcp-resource URI through its server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero downstream server/resource calls when disabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A resource read/watch could start a disabled server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fails before server startup or remote resource I/O

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured servers and gateway/tool/resource requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing server startup concurrency is unchanged; filtering is synchronous over the current server list and prevents disabled starts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Enablement is observable and workspace-server membership is a derived cached set over registry collections. Gateway filtering reads current enablement without introducing a separate cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: guards precede boundary operations and tests assert zero starts/calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server counts can vary, but filtering is linear over already-materialized in-memory entries and avoids much larger subprocess/network costs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; these changes reduce expensive boundary work for disabled servers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Forward local/workspace MCP servers to Copilot, Claude, or Codex Agent Host sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The bundler serializes server configuration and source metadata before customization synchronization; providers then filter workspace-sourced servers before runtime launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize MCP configuration plus per-server source metadata and hash bundle content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Linear in forwarded server count, once per bundle recomputation; unchanged bundles reuse nonce/content
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Bundles serialized configuration, cwd, and enablement but not source metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Synced customization bundling and provider plugin parsing paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bundle-level operations, not one new boundary per metadata entry
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same bundle transport existed without the small source map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before providers consume forwarded servers

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only enabled servers after class and per-server filtering
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workspace-forwarded servers were launched according to per-server enablement only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff prevents gated workspace servers from starting

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective forwarded MCP server count after delivery assessment and name grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Bundling iterates servers once and existing synchronization controls writes; provider launch filtering is in-memory per server.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stable content hashes/nonces reuse unchanged bundles; adding source metadata changes the nonce only when provenance changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serialization and stable nonce behavior are covered by changed code/tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large MCP inventories are uncommon; added metadata is one short source value per forwarded server.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the added linear metadata is bounded by the existing forwarded inventory and enables avoidance of much more expensive server launches.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 73 changed files and all diff pages. Traced local MCP gating, Agent Host metadata/IPC, forwarding, and Copilot/Claude/Codex launch paths. Submitted one medium repeated-I/O finding for Claude's duplicate uncached serial scan; other new work is bounded, cached/coalesced, or removes expensive server starts.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
